content.text: Salesforce case status updated New -> In Progress -> Escalated (Waiting on Another Department).
Case status updated Escalated -> Resolved.
Tech support case number 218550 shared; case later shown Resolved -> Closed.
Vishwas relayed a call from Keebler Thornton at UPS Haslet reporting the system had stopped at the bag-out stage after sorting.

Site believed a robot was involved and was trying to determine which robot it was; a similar problem had reportedly occurred the previous week. Site was trying to find what they believed was a robot out of sequence/position; this had occurred before according to the customer.
Case 00218550 opened 4/3/2025 4:28 AM. Subject: 'The system stopped at bag-out after sorting.' Priority 2-High: Production seriously impacted.
FORTNA Technical Support requested assistance on case 00218550 for UPS TXRTH Haslet (installation group 1G0011744).
Robots were turned off because batteries were low and would otherwise die out.
After joining the call, Ekram Nafis performed checks related to turning the robots back on.
The robots had been turned back on and were staying on so far.
Support explained that when an AGV with no tote is removed from the grid, it needs to be replaced with another one.
With all robots in proper sequence, the customer confirmed they were functional and the parties agreed to end the call.
Site reported AGV 202 was being taken out for good because it kept losing QR code; it had been pulled earlier and later added back when the system was messed up a couple weeks earlier.
Site reported Shane helped, but the system had not exchanged yet.
Site reported they were good after receiving help.
A 'Tipper 1 heartbeat' event was reported.
Site reported manually bagging out; informed support the site was handling the process manually and was at the close-out stage.

Tote 14 had gotten mixed around at the hospital and was read at hospital when it was actually in L385. Everything then ran smoothly, but during bagout it went into request and never progressed, so they manually bagged out.
Site was asked to remove and add AGV pairs so one pair would get bag-out started; bag-out then started, processed most items, and stopped again.
Teams chat: Keebler was asked to remove and add AGV pairs in each zone, hoping one pair would get bag-out started; bag-out started, bagged out most items, but stopped again.
Vishwas reported troubleshooting options had been exhausted and the earlier requested steps had already been performed.
Could not see the screen in Aveva; UPS had updated it. Suggested checking system active error.
Activity was checked and an AGV did not move for 3 hours at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH); exact AGV identifier not legible.
'The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault' followed by 'Should I unplug it?'
Advised: 'Hit acknowledge and try again. No.' (do not unplug) 'Is the tote ID 28?'
'Yes the tote at hospital is 28' and 'Yes Sir all good.'

Asked whether the HMI at site is being updated that day to cover the task issue; said it needs to happen ASAP along with a process to recover from a stuck task, and a debug process to identify a stuck task needs to be created before the next sort.
One of the prior night's errors, a stuck task, is only visible on that (hospital) HMI.
Confirmed: 'that is correct' -- the stuck-task-visible-only-on-that-HMI statement.
'I've got a message fault that I haven't seen and no stack light faults' with 'Bagging out!' shown nearby.
'202 needs taken out it is messed up it needs to be tagged for Geek.'
'I'll get it after bag out,' indicating deferred handling of unit 202 until bag-out completed.

Use the Hospital HMI / lane UI at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) to acknowledge a displayed fault, retry the operation without unplugging the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirm that the affected tote is tote 28, and verify that the site reports the condition as all good.

structured_payload.title: Hospital HMI / lane UI fault acknowledge-and-retry check
structured_payload.summary: Use the Hospital HMI / lane UI at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) to acknowledge a displayed fault, retry the operation without unplugging the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirm that the affected tote is tote 28, and verify that the site reports the condition as all good.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use this Hospital HMI / lane UI check when the Hospital HMI / lane UI displays a fault associated with a hospital-station tote and an acknowledge-and-retry response is appropriate.
not_for: Do not use this as a recovery sequence for a stuck task; the incident identifies a stuck-task visibility limitation on the Hospital HMI / lane UI but does not provide a reusable stuck-task recovery sequence.
Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI as a troubleshooting action.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Operate the Hospital HMI / lane UI, acknowledge the displayed fault, retry the operation, and confirm the tote and resulting site condition.
Provide remote guidance and review the result when the Hospital HMI / lane UI fault remains, tote 28 cannot be confirmed, or an all-good state cannot be reported.

safety_notes: Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI as a troubleshooting action.
Stop and escalate if the fault remains after acknowledge-and-retry.

access_required: Operator access to the Hospital HMI / lane UI at the affected hospital station.
system_preconditions: A fault is displayed on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.

visual_references.description: Hospital HMI / lane UI screenshot showing a small HMI-like tote screen with a red header and green list elements; text inside the crop is mostly unreadable.

steps.title: Inspect the displayed Hospital HMI / lane UI fault
steps.purpose: Confirm that the reported fault is present on the live Hospital HMI / lane UI before taking the acknowledge-and-retry action.
steps.instruction: Open the Hospital HMI / lane UI and inspect the live station screen for the reported fault. Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
steps.expected_result: The reported fault is visible on the Hospital HMI / lane UI and the live screen is available for interaction.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI remains displayed and usable, with the reported fault visible for acknowledgement.
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI cannot be accessed, the reported fault is not visible, or the screen is not usable for the next action.

actions.label: Inspect Hospital HMI / lane UI fault
actions.exact_action: Open the Hospital HMI / lane UI and confirm that the fault is displayed; do not unplug the HMI.

stop_or_escalate_if: The Hospital HMI / lane UI cannot be accessed or the fault is not visible.
The HMI appears to require unplugging; do not unplug it and escalate for further support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault; the HMI artifact is a small HMI-like tote screen with a red header and green list elements.
The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault ... Should I unplug it?

steps.title: Acknowledge the fault and retry the operation
steps.purpose: Apply the incident-supported acknowledge-and-retry response to the displayed Hospital HMI / lane UI fault.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, select the acknowledge control and retry the operation. Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI / lane UI accepts the acknowledgement and the operation enters a retry state rather than remaining blocked by the same displayed fault.
steps.healthy_condition: The retry proceeds on the Hospital HMI / lane UI without the reported fault continuing to block the operation.
steps.failure_condition: The acknowledgement or retry does not take effect, or the same fault remains after the retry.

actions.label: Acknowledge and retry
actions.exact_action: Select the HMI acknowledge control, then retry the operation.

stop_or_escalate_if: The Hospital HMI / lane UI does not accept the acknowledgement or retry.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Hit acknowledge and try again. No. Is the tote ID 28?

steps.title: Confirm tote 28 and the cleared Hospital HMI / lane UI state
steps.purpose: Validate that the retry addressed the affected tote and that the site condition is clear.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI and with the site contact, confirm that the tote at the hospital station is tote 28 and verify that the site reports the condition as all good.
steps.expected_result: The tote at the hospital station is confirmed as tote 28 and the site reports that everything is good.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI shows or supports confirmation of tote 28, and the site reports an all-good condition.
steps.failure_condition: Tote 28 cannot be confirmed, or the site cannot report an all-good condition after the retry.

actions.label: Confirm tote ID and cleared state
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the tote at the hospital station is tote 28 and verify that the site reports the condition as all good.

stop_or_escalate_if: The site cannot report an all-good state.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Yes the tote at hospital is 28. Yes Sir all good.

success_criteria: The Hospital HMI / lane UI fault is acknowledged.
The retry succeeds without unplugging the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
The tote at the hospital station is confirmed as tote 28.
The site reports that everything is good.
healthy_conditions: The Hospital HMI / lane UI is usable and no longer has the reported fault blocking the retried operation.
The affected tote is confirmed as tote 28.
The site reports an all-good condition.
failure_conditions: The Hospital HMI / lane UI fault remains after acknowledgement and retry.
The acknowledgement or retry does not take effect.
The site cannot report an all-good condition.
escalation_guidance: Stop and escalate to L2 support if the fault remains after acknowledge-and-retry.
Escalate if tote 28 cannot be confirmed or the site cannot report an all-good state.
Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
The incident identifies a stuck-task visibility limitation on this Hospital HMI / lane UI, but does not provide a reusable stuck-task recovery sequence.

content.text: Use this path when automated bag-out stops or progresses only partially and site personnel report that an AGV is not moving, a robot may be out of sequence, or a related HMI shows a fault.

structured_payload.title: Bag-out stoppage with unresponsive or out-of-sequence AGVs
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use this path when automated bag-out stops or progresses only partially and site personnel report that an AGV is not moving, a robot may be out of sequence, or a related HMI shows a fault.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Determine whether the bag-out stoppage is associated with an abnormal AGV, pairing or sequence state, or an HMI-visible task or tote condition; apply only source-supported authorized recovery direction; and confirm that AGVs and bag-out remain functional.
observed_entry_symptoms: Automated bag-out stops after sorting or starts and then stops before completion.
Manual bagging out is required because the automated process does not progress.
One or more AGVs or robots appear not to be moving.
The site reports that a robot may be out of sequence or out of position.
An HMI associated with the hospital area shows a fault or a task-related condition.

However, the exact fault, decisive action, and complete diagnostic evidence are incomplete or ambiguous.

nodes.title: Confirm automated bag-out stoppage and affected operating scope
nodes.intent: Confirm that automated bag-out is stopped or only partially progressing and determine whether the condition is site-wide, localized to a zone or pair, or limited to a tote or task.
nodes.goal: Confirm that automated bag-out is stopped or only partially progressing and determine whether the condition is site-wide, localized to a zone or pair, or limited to a tote or task.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to interview the site about whether automated bag-out is stopped, whether it started and stopped again, whether manual bagging is being used, and which affected zone, pair, tote, or task is involved; use the incident-supported RMS activity or status view when available to compare the affected operating scope.
nodes.source_supported_description: The case and chat evidence describe a bag-out stoppage after sorting, manual bagging, and a need to identify the affected robot or exchange pair.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about whether automated bag-out is stopped, whether it started and stopped again, whether manual bagging is being used, and which affected zone, pair, tote, or task is involved; use the incident-supported RMS activity or status view when available to compare the affected operating scope.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support observes the bag-out state through site reporting and available operational views. Unhealthy evidence is automated bag-out stopped, only partially completed, or requiring manual bagging; healthy evidence is automated bag-out progressing normally; inconclusive evidence is an unclear scope, unavailable view, or conflicting site reports.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Site reports described bag-out stopping, manual bagging, affected exchange pairs, and suspected robot involvement.
Page 11 contains an RMS-style artifact showing AGV activity evidence.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The incident includes an RMS-style activity observation showing an AGV did not move for three hours.

ontology_gaps: No supplied ontology mapping establishes a specific bag-out progress or exchange-pair status surface.
healthy_indicators: Site reports automated bag-out is progressing and does not require manual intervention.
The affected scope cannot be reproduced or is limited to a resolved transient condition.
unhealthy_indicators: Automated bag-out is stopped.
Bag-out starts but stops before completion.
Manual bagging out is required.
A specific zone, pair, tote, or task is identified as unable to progress.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot identify whether the condition is automated or manual.
The RMS or other operational view is unavailable or does not show enough detail to determine scope.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The system stopped at bag-out after sorting.
System is not going into bagout. Manual bagging out reported.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm from site reporting and any available operational views whether automated bag-out is stopped, only partially progressing, or not reproducibly occurring; identify the affected scope (site-wide vs localized to a zone/pair vs limited to a tote/task).
evidence_to_collect: Whether automated bag-out is currently stopped vs partially completed vs progressing normally (latest observation time).
Whether site is using manual bagging out (and since when).
What the site identifies as the affected scope: zone/pair vs tote/task (including any stated identifiers).
Any available RMS view evidence used to compare scope (e.g., RMS activity/status artifacts or fleet overview indicators).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Automated bag-out is progressing normally without requiring manual intervention; or the reported stoppage cannot be reproduced as an active issue.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Automated bag-out is stopped or only partially completed, requiring manual bagging; and the site can identify a specific affected scope (zone/pair or tote/task) that is unable to progress.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site cannot determine whether the issue is automated vs manual, or the RMS/operational view is unavailable/insufficient to determine affected scope; or reports conflict.
nodes.generated_guidance: Treat site statements as the initial truth for scope; do not assume a specific AGV/robot until later nodes. If bag-out is not reproducible, exit/retriage rather than entering recovery nodes.

nodes.title: Check for AGV inactivity or active fault evidence
nodes.intent: Determine whether one or more AGVs show abnormal inactivity, active error, or a related sequence or pairing indication that correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.goal: Determine whether one or more AGVs show abnormal inactivity, active error, or a related sequence or pairing indication that correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect RMS fleet activity and status for AGV movement, active fault indications, and sequence or pairing abnormalities, and to compare the affected AGV or pair with the bag-out stoppage; if the relevant screen is unavailable, use the source-mentioned system active-error view without assuming a specific backend field.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source explicitly records an RMS-style observation that an AGV did not move for three hours and preserves a discussion about checking system active error.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect RMS fleet activity and status for AGV movement, active fault indications, and sequence or pairing abnormalities, and to compare the affected AGV or pair with the bag-out stoppage; if the relevant screen is unavailable, use the source-mentioned system active-error view without assuming a specific backend field.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or L1 support observes the RMS activity or status view; support may also use the source-mentioned system active-error view when available. Unhealthy evidence is an AGV not moving for an extended period, an active robot fault, or a sequence or pairing indication associated with the stoppage; healthy evidence is normal movement and no relevant active fault; inconclusive evidence is an unreadable or unavailable view, unidentified AGV, or no correlation to bag-out.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The page 11 artifact is classified as an RMS screenshot and visibly supports the statement that an AGV did not move for three hours.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source reports an AGV that did not move for three hours and mentions checking system active error.

ontology_gaps: The supplied capability snippet lists backend models but does not provide a complete Stage 5 mapping for this incident's exact active-error evidence.
healthy_indicators: Affected AGVs show current movement or normal activity.
No relevant active AGV fault or sequence indication is present.
The bag-out stoppage does not correlate with AGV inactivity.
unhealthy_indicators: An AGV is shown as not moving for an extended period.
An active robot fault or abnormal sequence or pairing indication is present.
AGV inactivity or abnormal state corresponds with the stalled bag-out scope.
inconclusive_indicators: The AGV identifier or status details cannot be read.
RMS activity is stale, unavailable, or does not explain the bag-out condition.
Only a suspected out-of-sequence condition is reported without corroborating status evidence.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: An AGV did not move for 3 hours.
You can check system active error.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS activity/status for AGV movement inactivity and check for active fault evidence; corroborate with backend active error evidence to determine whether the bag-out stoppage correlates with one or more AGVs.
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/activity indicators showing whether one or more AGVs are not moving for an extended period.
Any visible active fault/alarm indication in RMS for the suspected AGVs/robots.
Backend corroboration: active error evidence for the same timeframe/scope using WCS/Helix DB read-only views (active AGV errors).
Whether the suspected inactivity/fault correlates with the bag-out stoppage scope (zone/pair/tote/task reported in node_1).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Affected AGVs show current movement/normal activity and no relevant active fault/sequence indication correlates with the stalled bag-out scope.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AGV/robot is shown as not moving for an extended period or has active fault evidence (active error / abnormal state) that correlates with the stalled bag-out scope and supports sequence/pairing abnormality hypothesis.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: AGV identifier/status details cannot be read, RMS activity evidence is stale/unavailable, or no correlation can be established with the bag-out stoppage.

optional_corroboration.note: If RMS shows an AGV fault/inactivity but backend active-error evidence is unavailable or ambiguous, stop at inconclusive and proceed to HMI/task investigation (node_3) rather than assuming a sequence/pairing recovery action.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Confirm AGV live state (including movement-related state, locations, and identifiers) from SSMS to corroborate RMS observations and check for active abnormal states.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: High combined score and clear match to AGV state inspection; used as the backend evidence path that pairs with RMS for system-state confirmation.
match_gaps: Node_2 emphasizes active error/fault evidence correlation; candidate is AGV state inspection (may still support ErrorCode/State, but not explicitly the exact 'active error' rubric).

nodes.generated_guidance: Use RMS to identify candidates (e.g., AGV not moving) but rely on SSMS read-only evidence to corroborate active error presence and state freshness. Do not decide to recover AGV sequence/pairing solely on a single RMS screenshot.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the source-named hospital-area HMI for the displayed fault, task state, tote identity or location indication, and whether the workflow request progresses; include the approved HMI acknowledgement or retry decision rubric without prescribing exact screen navigation or physical disconnection.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports a hospital HMI fault, a tote read at an unexpected location, a stuck task visible only on that HMI, and guidance to acknowledge and try again.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the source-named hospital-area HMI for the displayed fault, task state, tote identity or location indication, and whether the workflow request progresses; include the approved HMI acknowledgement or retry decision rubric without prescribing exact screen navigation or physical disconnection.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes the named HMI or hospital-area interface. Unhealthy evidence is a displayed fault, stuck task, tote mismatch or location discrepancy, or a request that does not progress; healthy evidence is no relevant HMI fault and normal task or tote progression; inconclusive evidence is an unreadable screen, an HMI that cannot be reached, or a reported fault whose relationship to bag-out is unclear.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Chat states that the HMI at the hospital was showing a fault and later references the HMI as the location of a stuck task.
Chat states that the team could not see the screen in Aveva.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippets do not provide a validated HMI task or tote-state mapping for this incident.
healthy_indicators: The HMI shows no relevant fault or stuck task.
The relevant tote or task is correctly identified and the workflow request progresses.
The site confirms the HMI-related condition is no longer blocking operation.
unhealthy_indicators: The HMI shows a fault.
A stuck task is visible only on the HMI.
A tote is reported at an unexpected location or the request enters a state but does not progress.
inconclusive_indicators: The HMI screen is unavailable, unreadable, or not updated.
The referenced hospital area cannot be reconciled with the ingestion site metadata.
The fault is visible but its relationship to the bag-out stoppage is not established.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect the hospital-area HMI for the displayed fault/stuck task/tote mismatch indication and determine whether that HMI-visible condition is actively blocking bag-out progression; follow the approved acknowledge/retry decision rubric as supported by the linked HMI procedure.
nodes.primary_surface: hospital_hmi (and Aveva/operational view only if it corresponds to the same HMI evidence)
evidence_to_collect: Whether the hospital HMI is reachable and readable (timestamp / last update).
Which specific fault/task state is displayed (fault code/text or fault category).
Whether a tote/task identity/location mismatch is displayed (tote readout, lane/tote location indication).
Whether workflow request/bag-out progresses after the approved acknowledge/retry action.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant HMI fault/stuck task/tote mismatch is displayed; the relevant tote/task is correctly identified and the workflow request progresses.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital HMI shows a fault or a stuck task (or tote/location mismatch) and the workflow request does not progress accordingly.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: HMI screen is unavailable/unreadable/not updated, or the relationship between the visible fault and bag-out stoppage cannot be established.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not replace diagnostic interpretation with remediation. If the HMI is unavailable/unreadable, do not invent a fault cause—route to escalation (node_6) if no other supported evidence path is available.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — LatticeCodeModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.67 supplied real column names and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model LatticeCodeModel (geek_agv): Stores the lattice codes and their respective station IDs; when a tote is inducted or dropped off, Geek requires a lattice code for the location, and the Geek Comm module uses this table to convert the StationId from a robotics-module request into the lattice code Geek requires.. Fields: Id: Row id.; EntityInserted: Insert timestamp.; EntityLastUpdate: Last update timestamp.; StationId: Respective station ID that maps to the lattice code.; LatticeCode: Lattice

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — RobotDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.; ToteId: Tote currently

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — E-stop / safety stop
ontology_evidence.text: Capability e_stop_or_safety_stop: Confirm physical E-stop / safety stop state and coordinate on-site reset.. When: Emergency stop depressed, safety circuit, master E-stop clear prep. Not for: RMS soft stop / PauseAGVs (rms_soft_stop).. Surfaces: physical_floor, site_interview, rms_ui, wcs_sql, aveva_hmi. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: sorter_sweeper. Models: EstopModel. APIs: . Key fields: EstopModel.Name: ESTOP name.; EstopModel.Geek AreaId: Geek area id for the ESTOP zone.; E

nodes.title: Restore the affected AGV sequence or pairing state through an authorized recovery path
nodes.intent: Use an approved, role-authorized recovery procedure to restore the affected AGV or pair to a valid operating sequence when the diagnostic evidence supports that direction.
nodes.goal: Use an approved, role-authorized recovery procedure to restore the affected AGV or pair to a valid operating sequence when the diagnostic evidence supports that direction.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized AGV sequence, pairing, removal, replacement, or controlled return-to-operation recovery, including the requirement that an AGV removed from the grid be appropriately replaced and that safety and role limits be respected; do not infer a specific robot or exact recovery action.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support asked the site to remove and add AGV pairs; the source also states that a removed AGV without a tote must be replaced and later reports robots in proper sequence.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized AGV sequence, pairing, removal, replacement, or controlled return-to-operation recovery, including the requirement that an AGV removed from the grid be appropriately replaced and that safety and role limits be respected; do not infer a specific robot or exact recovery action.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L2 support or another authorized role records that the approved recovery path was completed. Progress evidence is that affected robots remain on, the relevant sequence or pairing state is restored, and bag-out can proceed; failure evidence is continued inactivity, repeated stopping, or an unresolved sequence or pairing condition; inconclusive evidence is that the exact recovery action or resulting state cannot be verified.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages directed removal and addition of AGV pairs and discussed restoring robots to proper sequence.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not establish the exact authorized AGV recovery procedure or the decisive action used in this case.
healthy_indicators: Authorized personnel confirm the affected AGV or pair is in the expected sequence.
Robots remain on and available after the approved recovery.
The recovery path reports completion without introducing a new fault.
unhealthy_indicators: The affected AGV or pair remains out of sequence or unavailable.
Robots turn off again or remain unable to support bag-out.
Bag-out starts but stops again after the recovery attempt.
inconclusive_indicators: The source does not identify which action restored service.
The sequence or pairing state cannot be confirmed.
The role authorized to perform the recovery is unavailable.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not proceed with physical or state-changing recovery unless the role, safety conditions, and approved procedure are established.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Asked the site to remove and add AGV pairs; bag-out started, processed most, then stopped.
When all robots were in proper sequence, the customer confirmed they were functional.

nodes.primary_action: Restore the affected AGV sequence/pairing or related AGV operating state using an authorized recovery procedure consistent with the diagnostic evidence, ensuring any removed AGV is appropriately replaced and roles/safety limits are respected.
evidence_to_collect: Confirmation that an authorized recovery path (sequence/pairing restoration) was executed.
Evidence that the affected robots/pairs remain on and the relevant sequence/pairing state is restored.
Whether bag-out begins progressing again after recovery attempt (site confirmation or observable operational evidence).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Authorized personnel confirm the affected AGV/pair is back in the expected sequence and remains available; recovery completed without introducing a new fault.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Affected AGV/pair remains out of sequence/unavailable; robots turn off again or cannot support bag-out; bag-out starts but stops again after recovery attempt.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The source does not specify which exact recovery action restored service, or sequence/pairing confirmation cannot be verified, or authorized role is unavailable.

optional_corroboration.note: After any sequence/pairing recovery, validate sustained operation in node_5 using RMS and hospital-area HMI evidence; do not treat a single improvement as stable recovery.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Hospital HMI / lane UI fault acknowledge-and-retry check
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Acknowledge the hospital HMI fault and verify whether retry clears the non-progressing workflow condition.
linked_primary_procedure.required_role: L2_support / L3_support (per role constraints; verify authorization at runtime)
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: This is a case-local candidate and explicitly matches the incident note about acknowledge-and-try-again guidance, aligning with node_4’s requirement to restore state via an authorized recovery path when HMI faults were identified.
match_gaps: Node_4 primary intent is AGV sequence/pairing state restoration; selected procedure targets HMI acknowledge/retry rather than explicit AGV sequence restoration.

nodes.generated_guidance: Only apply state-changing recovery once diagnosis evidence supports the direction (AGV inactivity/active error OR hospital HMI fault blocking). Ensure any AGV removed from the grid is replaced to preserve the operating sequence.

ontology_evidence.evidence_relation: Recovery involves removing/re-adding or controlled return-to-operation steps when AGVs/pairs are out of sequence.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Recovery execution is required; however, the packet does not specify the exact decisive recovery action. Use an authorized recovery procedure matching the diagnosed evidence (AGV inactivity/active error vs HMI fault blocking).

nodes.intent: Confirm that the recovery restored the affected workflow and that AGVs remain functional rather than merely showing a temporary improvement.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the recovery restored the affected workflow and that AGVs remain functional rather than merely showing a temporary improvement.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate sustained AGV availability and sequence state through the source-supported RMS activity view, confirm bag-out progress with the site, and check the relevant hospital-area HMI for recurrence of the fault or stuck-task indication before declaring recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records customer confirmation that robots were functional in proper sequence and a later all-good response after HMI-related troubleshooting.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate sustained AGV availability and sequence state through the source-supported RMS activity view, confirm bag-out progress with the site, and check the relevant hospital-area HMI for recurrence of the fault or stuck-task indication before declaring recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms automated bag-out progress and normal AGV operation, while support observes the available RMS or HMI status. Healthy evidence is AGVs moving or available, the relevant sequence or pairing state remaining valid, bag-out completing or continuing normally, and no relevant HMI fault; unhealthy evidence is renewed inactivity, another partial bag-out stop, or a recurring task or HMI fault; inconclusive evidence is only a verbal improvement without observable continued operation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The incident includes an RMS-style activity view used to identify an AGV that had not moved.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source used AGV activity and active-error discussion as evidence during troubleshooting.

ontology_gaps: No supplied ontology mapping defines a complete automated bag-out validation contract.
healthy_indicators: The customer confirms AGVs are functional.
AGVs remain available or moving after recovery.
Automated bag-out continues or completes without another stoppage.
The relevant HMI no longer shows the blocking fault or stuck task.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV inactivity returns.
Bag-out stops again after partial progress.
The HMI fault or stuck task recurs.
The affected sequence or pairing state is not maintained.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a temporary 'all good' report is available.
No continued bag-out or AGV activity can be observed.
The HMI or RMS view remains unavailable.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not declare recovery from a temporary improvement alone; use the escalation path if stable operation cannot be demonstrated.

nodes.primary_action: Validate stable AGV operation and sustained automated bag-out after the recovery attempt by checking RMS activity and the relevant hospital-area HMI, confirming that the fault/stuck task does not recur.
evidence_to_collect: RMS evidence that AGVs are moving/available and that the relevant sequence/pairing state remains valid after recovery.
Whether automated bag-out continues progressing or completes normally.
Hospital-area HMI evidence: blocking fault/stuck task is no longer shown.
Site/customer confirmation that operations are stable (not just a temporary acknowledgement).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: AGVs remain functional and available; automated bag-out continues or completes normally; hospital HMI no longer shows the blocking fault/stuck task.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: AGV inactivity returns; bag-out stops again after partial progress; hospital HMI fault/stuck task recurs; sequence/pairing state is not maintained.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a temporary 'all good' verbal report is available; continued operation cannot be observed; RMS/HMI views remain unavailable.

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV active errors
ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_active_errors: Confirm whether AGVs/robots currently have active error or fault state.. When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {"diagnostic_surfaces": ["wcs_sql", "wcs_api", "rms_ui"], "control_surfaces": ["wcs_api"

Not for: Generic site stoppage without bag-out evidence.. Surfaces: wcs_sql, wcs_api, apidog, rms_ui, site_interview. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: sorter_sweeper. nodes.title: Determine whether an AGV active error or abnormal fleet state is present
nodes.intent: Determine whether an AGV, robot, or system active-error condition correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.goal: Determine whether an AGV, robot, or system active-error condition correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet and activity views for active AGV faults, prolonged inactivity, unavailable robots, and abnormal status associated with the affected bag-out flow, and to review the source-named system active-error view when available. The procedure should define how to interpret an active error versus an unavailable or merely idle robot without prescribing commands.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support reported checking activity and finding an AGV that had not moved for three hours, while the discussion also referred to checking system active error because the Aveva screen was not visible.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet and activity views for active AGV faults, prolonged inactivity, unavailable robots, and abnormal status associated with the affected bag-out flow, and to review the source-named system active-error view when available. The procedure should define how to interpret an active error versus an unavailable or merely idle robot without prescribing commands.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or L1 support reviews RMS fleet/activity status and, where available to the support role, the system active-error view. Unhealthy signals are an active AGV fault, prolonged inactivity, or an abnormal robot status associated with the stalled workflow. Healthy signal is no active error and expected movement or availability. Inconclusive means the active-error view is unavailable, the robot cannot be identified, or the evidence does not correlate with the stoppage.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The page 11 artifact is an RMS-style screenshot showing an AGV that did not move for three hours.
The incident discussion says the screen could not be seen in Aveva and suggested checking system active error.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source explicitly references checking system active error and provides RMS evidence of prolonged AGV inactivity.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a validated backend mapping for the source-named system active-error view.
healthy_indicators: No relevant active AGV error is displayed.
The affected AGV or pair shows expected activity and availability.
unhealthy_indicators: An active AGV or system error is displayed.
The affected AGV remains inactive or unavailable.
The fleet view indicates a robot state inconsistent with the bag-out workflow.
inconclusive_indicators: The Aveva or system active-error screen cannot be viewed.
RMS activity data is stale or the affected AGV cannot be identified.
The displayed error cannot be correlated to the bag-out symptom.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: I checked the activity and see an AGV didn't move for 3 hours.
Page context mentions checking system active error; the cropped technical view is not readable.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS fleet/activity evidence for active AGV faults, prolonged inactivity, and abnormal robot availability, and corroborate with backend active-error evidence when available; avoid prescribing robot commands based solely on inactivity.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS fleet/activity views (rms_ui) + WCS/SSMS read-only active-error evidence (wcs_sql)
evidence_to_collect: RMS indicates any active AGV error/faults or abnormal availability for the affected operational area
RMS indicates prolonged inactivity for one or more AGVs/robots
Whether a system/active-error screen is visible to support correlation
WCS/SSMS (robotics database) active error evidence for current active errors (if RMS evidence indicates faults or stoppage needs corroboration)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant active AGV/system error correlates with the stoppage; affected AGVs show expected activity/availability in RMS.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Active AGV/system error correlates with bag-out stoppage, or affected AGVs remain inactive/unavailable; fleet/robot state appears inconsistent with the bag-out workflow.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Active-error evidence is unavailable (e.g., backend screen cannot be accessed, RMS data is stale, or the displayed error cannot be correlated to the bag-out symptom).

optional_corroboration.note: If the Aveva/system active-error view is unreadable or not accessible, use WCS/SSMS read-only active-error models to preserve evidence integrity before escalating.

nodes.generated_guidance: Interpretation rule: distinguish an 'active error present' state from 'robot unavailable/idle' without assuming causality. Correlate: stoppage timing + RMS inactivity + backend active-error presence/absence.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — RobotDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.; ToteId: Tote currently

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV active errors
ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_active_errors: Confirm whether AGVs/robots currently have active error or fault state.. When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {"diagnostic_surfaces": ["wcs_sql", "wcs_api", "rms_ui"], "control_surfaces": ["wcs_api"

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — Fleet / overall system status
ontology_evidence.text: Capability fleet_system_status: Confirm overall fleet / system-down vs running from overview surfaces.. When: Blank RMS, site-wide stoppage report, overall system page down. Not for: Single-AGV active error deep dive without overall context.. Surfaces: rms_ui, aveva_hmi, event_viewer, wcs_sql, site_interview. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: SystemDatabaseModel, SystemStateModel, SortModel. APIs: SystemState. Key fields: SystemDatabaseModel.Id: R

nodes.intent: Distinguish an AGV sequence or pairing concern from a tote or task condition visible through the hospital-area HMI.
nodes.goal: Distinguish an AGV sequence or pairing concern from a tote or task condition visible through the hospital-area HMI.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Decision-rubric procedure needed to compare the site-reported sequence or pairing concern with the hospital HMI's visible fault or task state, the tote identity and physical location, and the RMS activity observation. The procedure should define when a reported HMI fault or tote mismatch is relevant to bag-out and when it should be treated as unconfirmed.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports a tote read at the hospital while physically elsewhere, a hospital HMI fault, a stuck task visible only on that HMI, and a suspected robot out-of-sequence condition. These remain source-supported observations and hypotheses rather than confirmed cause.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Decision-rubric procedure needed to compare the site-reported sequence or pairing concern with the hospital HMI's visible fault or task state, the tote identity and physical location, and the RMS activity observation. The procedure should define when a reported HMI fault or tote mismatch is relevant to bag-out and when it should be treated as unconfirmed.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site/operator checks the relevant hospital HMI and reports whether it shows a fault, a stuck task, or a tote identity/state inconsistent with the physical workflow; support correlates that report with RMS activity and the bag-out symptom. Unhealthy-style signals are a reported stuck task, HMI fault, or tote read in an unexpected location. Healthy-style signal is no such condition and the robot or pair is operating normally. Inconclusive means the HMI is unavailable, the fault text is unreadable, or the tote/task relationship cannot be confirmed.

healthy_indicators: The hospital HMI shows no relevant fault or stuck task.

nodes.primary_action: Use the hospital HMI fault/task display and tote/task context (as observable by the site) to decide whether the bag-out stoppage is better explained by sequence/pairing inconsistency vs a tote/task/HMI blocking condition; treat HMI observations as confirmed only when they can be correlated to RMS activity evidence.
evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI fault/stuck-task indication visibility (fault text readable or not)
Whether the hospital HMI shows a tote identity/state and whether it conflicts with physical location or with RMS-backed tote/robot correlation
Site/operator description of the suspected out-of-sequence/out-of-position robot/pair (if any)
RMS activity evidence indicating whether the robot/pair is behaving normally or not during the same time window
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Hospital HMI shows no relevant fault/stuck task; tote identity/state matches physical workflow; robot/pair observations are consistent with normal operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital HMI shows fault/stuck task OR tote read is in an unexpected location OR site reports sequence/pair inconsistency that correlates with RMS activity.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Hospital HMI cannot be viewed/read reliably or tote/task relationship cannot be confirmed; the evidence cannot establish whether the condition is causal for bag-out stoppage.

optional_corroboration.note: If hospital HMI evidence is ambiguous, corroborate with backend robot/tote state where the tote/task identity can be established—otherwise treat as unconfirmed and prepare escalation.

nodes.generated_guidance: This node is a decision rubric node. Do not treat site-hypotheses (e.g., 'robot out of sequence') as confirmed until it is correlated with RMS activity/state and/or backend evidence that matches the same identifiers (when available).

nodes.title: Apply authorized recovery for the identified AGV or sequence condition
nodes.intent: Use the approved recovery path appropriate to the confirmed condition, such as restoring robot availability, correcting an AGV pair or sequence state, or handling a confirmed task or HMI condition.
nodes.goal: Use the approved recovery path appropriate to the confirmed condition, such as restoring robot availability, correcting an AGV pair or sequence state, or handling a confirmed task or HMI condition.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnostic evidence, including applicable AGV pair remove/add or replacement handling, robot availability and battery prerequisites, hospital HMI fault acknowledgement or retry when authorized, and any approved stuck-task recovery boundaries. The procedure must define role limits and must not assume that a specific robot or root cause has been confirmed.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident records robots being turned off because of low batteries, later turned back on, AGV pairs being removed and added, and advice to acknowledge and retry an HMI fault. The source does not isolate which action produced the final recovery.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnostic evidence, including applicable AGV pair remove/add or replacement handling, robot availability and battery prerequisites, hospital HMI fault acknowledgement or retry when authorized, and any approved stuck-task recovery boundaries. The procedure must define role limits and must not assume that a specific robot or root cause has been confirmed.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site or support role completes the applicable recovery procedure. A recovery-progress signal is that affected robots remain powered and available, the relevant pair or sequence is restored, or the identified task/tote condition is cleared. An unhealthy signal is that the same AGV or task remains unavailable or bag-out stops again. Inconclusive means the source-supported recovery option is not authorized, the condition cannot be identified, or the procedure outcome cannot be observed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source records guidance to acknowledge the HMI fault and try again.
The source records removing and adding AGV pairs in zones and checking AGV activity in an RMS-style view.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippets do not establish a complete capability mapping for the source-described pair replacement, HMI acknowledgement, or stuck-task recovery procedure.

unhealthy_indicators: A robot remains unavailable or repeatedly powers off.
Bag-out starts and stops again.
The HMI fault or suspected stuck task remains present.
inconclusive_indicators: The applicable recovery path cannot be selected from available evidence.

Recovery was attempted but its effect cannot be observed.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not perform physical removal, pair changes, or other state-changing actions without the applicable approved procedure and role authorization.

nodes.primary_action: Execute the approved authorized recovery appropriate to the selected diagnostic evidence (restoring robot availability, correcting an AGV pair/sequence state, and/or acknowledging/retrying the hospital HMI fault), within role authorization limits; do not assume a specific robot/root cause not confirmed by evidence.

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Affected robots/pair/sequence return to availability/state consistent with bag-out; hospital HMI fault/task indication clears without unsafe intervention.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Robots remain unavailable or repeatedly power off; bag-out starts then stops again; HMI fault/task indication persists.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The recovery path cannot be selected from available evidence; the action exceeds role authorization; or the outcome cannot be observed/verified.

optional_corroboration.note: If recovery involves any AGV availability restoration or pairing adjustments, corroborate before/after state with RMS overview and backend evidence to ensure it is not a transient UI-only change.

nodes.title: Validate restored sequence and sustained bag-out operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that robots are functional, the relevant sequence is stable, and bag-out completes or continues normally without immediate recurrence.
nodes.goal: Confirm that robots are functional, the relevant sequence is stable, and bag-out completes or continues normally without immediate recurrence.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate the recovered workflow by observing bag-out progress, confirming robot movement and sequence through the RMS activity/status view when available, checking that any relevant HMI fault or task indication is cleared, and obtaining site confirmation that automated operation remains functional before declaring recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source states that with all robots in proper sequence the customer confirmed they were functional. It also records a temporary bag-out restart followed by another stop, so sustained validation is necessary.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate the recovered workflow by observing bag-out progress, confirming robot movement and sequence through the RMS activity/status view when available, checking that any relevant HMI fault or task indication is cleared, and obtaining site confirmation that automated operation remains functional before declaring recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site/operator observes the bag-out workflow and confirms that robots are functional and remain in proper sequence; RMS activity, when available, shows expected movement. Healthy signals are automated bag-out progress, stable robot availability, and customer confirmation that operation is functional. Unhealthy signals are another stoppage, renewed prolonged inactivity, unresolved HMI fault, or a task that remains stuck. Inconclusive means only a temporary improvement is observed or the site cannot monitor the next workflow phase.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The incident includes an RMS-style activity screenshot used to observe AGV movement.
The incident includes an HMI artifact and reports that the tote/HMI condition was good after the troubleshooting exchange.
The customer confirmed that the robots were functional when all robots were in proper sequence.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: RMS activity and active-error observations are the source-supported means of corroborating that the AGV abnormal state has cleared.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not establish a validated mapping for complete bag-out or hospital-HMI task validation.
healthy_indicators: The site confirms robots are functional.
Robots remain in proper sequence and show expected activity.
Bag-out proceeds without returning to manual handling.
The relevant HMI fault or stuck-task indication is no longer present.
unhealthy_indicators: Bag-out stops again or remains incomplete.
An AGV again shows prolonged inactivity or an active error.
The HMI fault or stuck task persists.
The site cannot confirm functional automated operation.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a short period of robot uptime is observed.
Bag-out has not reached the relevant validation point.
RMS or HMI evidence is unavailable or unreadable.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: With all the robots in proper sequence the customer confirms that they are functional.
Bag-out started, processed most items, but stopped again.
The tote at the hospital was identified and the site reported that all was good.

nodes.primary_action: Validate sustained recovery by observing bag-out progress and confirming that robots are functional and remain in the relevant sequence; corroborate with RMS activity/state when available and verify any related HMI fault/stuck-task indication is cleared.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS UI (rms_ui) and/or Hospital HMI (hospital_hmi) plus site confirmation
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation that robots are functional and remain in proper sequence
Bag-out proceeds automatically without immediate recurrence (no need for manual bagging)
RMS activity/state shows expected robot movement and availability (when accessible)
Hospital HMI fault/stuck-task indication is cleared/absent (when applicable)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Automated bag-out proceeds normally with stable robot availability; no recurrence; HMI indication clears.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Bag-out stops again; an AGV becomes inactive again; HMI fault/stuck-task persists/unresolved.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only temporary improvement is observed or the next workflow phase cannot be monitored; RMS/HMI evidence is unavailable/readable.

optional_corroboration.note: If bag-out stops again shortly after recovery, re-run the evidence correlation (node_2 + node_3) rather than repeating recovery actions blindly.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do a time-bounded validation window. Success requires sustained operation, not just immediate restart.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with RMS activity and active-error evidence, HMI fault or stuck-task evidence, bag-out behavior, AGV sequence or pair changes attempted, robot power or availability observations, tote observations, validation results, and the limits or authorization constraints that prevented further action.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records that available troubleshooting options were exhausted at one point, that a prior pair adjustment only temporarily restored bag-out, and that the HMI/task issue required follow-up.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with RMS activity and active-error evidence, HMI fault or stuck-task evidence, bag-out behavior, AGV sequence or pair changes attempted, robot power or availability observations, tote observations, validation results, and the limits or authorization constraints that prevented further action.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1 support or the authorized site role determines that diagnostics are unavailable, the condition recurs after recovery, the HMI/task state remains unresolved, or the next action requires a role or procedure not available to the current responder. Healthy outcome for this gate is that escalation is not needed because validation passes. Unhealthy outcome is unresolved or recurring operation. Inconclusive outcome is insufficient evidence to determine whether the system is stable.

healthy_indicators: The supported recovery path restores stable automated operation and no handoff is required.
unhealthy_indicators: Bag-out remains stopped or stops again.
The AGV, task, tote, or HMI condition remains unresolved.
Further action requires an unavailable role or unsupported procedure.
inconclusive_indicators: Evidence is insufficient to identify the affected component or validate recovery.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Escalate for unresolved or unauthorized technical continuation, not merely because the historical incident involved collaboration or a prior case escalation.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The team reported that available options had been exhausted.

nodes.primary_action: Prepare escalation handoff by compiling attainable evidence: RMS activity overview, backend active-error evidence status (if attempted), hospital HMI fault/stuck-task evidence, bag-out behavior timeline, and any authorized recovery actions/attempt outcomes—then stop further unsupported or unauthorized state-changing actions.
nodes.primary_surface: Evidence collection across RMS UI + Hospital HMI + site confirmation (no new state changes)
evidence_to_collect: RMS activity/state evidence supporting where/when bag-out stalled
Backend active-error evidence collected or explicitly unavailable (attempted status)
Hospital HMI fault/stuck-task evidence (readable vs unreadable; timestamps if possible)
Site timeline: what was attempted (e.g., pair remove/add, robot power change, HMI acknowledge/retry) and what the observed outcomes were
Validation outcome (pass/fail/temporary improvement/insufficient monitoring window)
Authorization/role constraints that limited next actions
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Validation passes or the supported troubleshooting path restored stable operation, so escalation is not needed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Bag-out remains stopped/stops again; affected condition remains unresolved; next required action exceeds available authorization or evidence.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence is insufficient to identify the affected component or to confirm stable recovery, but escalation evidence packet is prepared.

optional_corroboration.note: If backend evidence was unavailable, include connectivity/service-health constraints in the handoff to avoid repeating the same inaccessible checks.

nodes.generated_guidance: This is a handoff preparation gate. Do not continue attempting state changes without a clear, evidence-supported recovery path and role authorization.
nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Escalation decision made because evidence and/or authorization is insufficient for further safe continuation.
